title: Latency-Aware Selective Verification in Generate–Validate NetOps Pipelines: A Preregistered Paired Study with gpt-5-mini
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (CAND-2026-001) to test whether a selective, low-latency verification tier (risk scoring + fast validator) inserted into a generate–validate–repair NetOps pipeline reduces unsafe commits from LLM-generated configuration proposals while meeting an operational latency SLO. Using a deterministic synthetic intent corpus of 400 paired operator intents (10% deterministic adversarial/OOD variants), all LLM generations used gpt-5-mini and scoring used a deterministic NetOps validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Results (artifact-backed): baseline proposals valid = 399/400; guarded (selective verifier) proposals valid = 400/400. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Execution accounting (artifact-backed) records 401 model calls used (400 shared-initial generations + 1 repair invocation) consistent with the preregistered shared-initial design (independent_condition_generation=false). The preregistered latency hypothesis (H2: 95th-percentile ≤ 2000 ms) cannot be evaluated from the archived confirmatory artifacts because end-to-end latency telemetry is not present in the provided execution outputs; this unresolved item and the shared-initial design’s inferential scope are described explicitly and with artifact references. All raw outputs, per-task scorer JSON, validator traces, provider-call logs, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA-256 hashes; paths and authoritative hashes are cited in the Disclosure Statement and within the paper for reproducibility.

sections.introduction: Automated intent→configuration translation promises faster, more consistent network change workflows. Recent work combines LLM generation with verification, repair, and digital-twin validation to reduce outages, yet operators must balance verification latency against safety. We preregistered CAND-2026-001 to test a latency-aware selective-verifier intervention ("guarded") that risk-scores proposals and sends only high-risk cases to a fast verifier, comparing it in a paired design to an LLM-only baseline. The design emphasizes operational realism while preserving rigorous preregistration: fixed task bank (400 intents), deterministic scorer/validator, and archived, hash-summed execution artifacts. The paper reports artifact-grounded outcomes, reconciles execution accounting, and explicitly records what preregistered hypotheses could not be evaluated from the archived run.
sections.related_work: Previous work has explored LLM-driven configuration generation, verifier-augmented repair loops, and agentic NetOps systems that employ digital twins and formal verification. Representative recent efforts include Cornetto and related configuration-repair benchmarks that use formal verification to measure regressions and agentic architectures that iterate with validators to improve safety. Our contribution is not a new verifier or benchmark but a preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation of a latency-aware selective verification intervention with full execution provenance and deterministic reconciliation to isolate verifier efficacy under a shared-generation design.
sections.methodology: Preregistration (CAND-2026-001) froze the study ID, hypotheses, estimands, sampling plan, retry/missingness rules, and analysis scripts prior to seeing confirmatory results. Key preregistered elements: 400 paired intents, 10% deterministic adversarial/OOD variants, model = gpt-5-mini, deterministic scorer = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, primary test = exact McNemar two-sided, and paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Execution contract set independent_condition_generation=false (shared-initial candidate reused across conditions) and initial_generation_calls_per_task=1. All generated outputs, per-task scorer JSONs, validator traces, and provider-call logs were archived; the execution manifest enumerates these artifacts and records SHA-256 hashes. The selective-verifier intervention was implemented per the preregistered pipeline; no post-hoc changes were applied. Missingness/retry policy: provider transient failures retried as preregistered; incomplete pairs due to unrecovered infrastructure failures would have been excluded (none occurred). Deterministic reconciliation checks were run and passed (see analysis artifacts).
sections.results: Execution and scoring (artifact-backed): completed pairs = 400; baseline valid proposals = 399/400 (0.9975); guarded valid proposals = 400/400 (1.000). Paired contingency (guarded × baseline): n11 = 399, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Primary estimand = 0.0025 (guarded minus baseline). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI for difference = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Execution accounting reconciles planned and observed model calls: planned_model_calls was 800 in the preregistration, but observed model_calls_used = 401; this is artifact-backed and explained by the preregistered shared-initial design which deterministically generates and reuses one shared candidate per intent across both conditions, producing 400 shared_initial_generation calls plus one repair call observed in this run (provider-call audit and execution manifest show stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 400, "repair": 1} and model_calls_used = 401). The single discordant episode (n10 = 1) and all per-episode scoring/validator traces are archived for inspection (paired_contingency_table.csv; per-episode scorer JSONs and response files are present under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/, hashes in the execution manifest).
sections.discussion: Interpretation: In this synthetic confirmatory corpus baseline proposals were near-ceiling for the deterministic validator; the guarded pipeline produced one additional valid outcome (absolute gain 0.25 percentage points). The observed marginal safety gain is small in this corpus and not statistically distinguishable from zero given the discordance pattern (n10=1, n01=0). Practical implication: selective verification may deliver larger safety gains in settings where baseline LLM correctness is lower, validators disagree more, or adversarial/OOD distributions are more prevalent. Design trade-offs: the preregistered shared-initial design (independent_condition_generation=false) reduces generation variance between conditions and isolates verifier/repair effects; it also materially reduced model call counts (401 observed calls vs the 800 planned under independent-generation). We preregistered that design choice and we document its inferential consequences: the estimand targets the verifier effect conditional on a shared initial candidate, not the joint effect of independent generation plus verification. Reproducibility and artifacts: all raw outputs, per-task scoring JSON, validator traces, provider-call logs, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA-256 hashes in the execution manifest (see Disclosure Statement). Unresolved preregistered item: H2 (latency SLO, 95th-percentile ≤ 2000 ms) could not be evaluated because end-to-end latency telemetry is not present in the confirmatory artifact bundle; the absence is artifact-backed (see execution/execution_log.jsonl and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl hashes) and is reported transparently rather than patched with synthetic telemetry. Recommendations: follow-up runs should (i) include full end-to-end latency telemetry and compare to a full-checker baseline, (ii) evaluate multiple LLMs and validators, (iii) sweep risk-classifier thresholds on adversarial/OOD distributions to map the verification-budget vs safety Pareto frontier, and (iv) test independent-condition generation if the operational setting requires separate generations per approval path.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a selective low-latency verifier with LLM-only generation. Artifact-backed primary analysis on 400 paired synthetic intents showed baseline = 399/400 valid and guarded = 400/400 valid; paired difference = 0.0025 (95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0075], exact McNemar p = 1.0). The run is fully archived with detailed validator and provider-call traces and deterministic reconciliation. The preregistered latency hypothesis (H2) could not be evaluated from the confirmatory artifacts due to absent latency telemetry; this unresolved item and the shared-initial design’s inferential scope are disclosed explicitly. We release the artifact hashes and encourage follow-up experiments that measure latency and adversarial robustness across models and validators before operational deployment.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure Statement (artifact-backed):
- Initial master prompt: archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). - Models and orchestration: declared model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json, SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Provider adapter family recorded as hosted_netops_gvr_v1; execution mode = scientific_confirmatory.
- Preregistration: CAND-2026-001 froze hypotheses, estimands, sampling plan, analysis scripts, and retry/missingness policy prior to observing confirmatory results. Preregistration SHA-256: 086d248e89636e99e788232e78a99b63459648545e6e79ed763c29521f8f8572 (recorded in the prereregistration and execution contract in the artifact bundle).
- Validator and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 served as the full-checker ground truth and scorer (scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation). Per-episode scorer JSONs and validator traces are archived under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/ with SHA-256 hashes listed in the execution manifest artifact_hashes.
- Execution manifest and provider-call audit: the run completed 800 episodes (400 paired intents × 2 conditions) and recorded model_calls_used = 401. The provider-call audit in the execution manifest documents stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 400, "repair": 1} and condition_counts = {"shared": 400, "guarded": 1}. The execution log file execution/execution_log.jsonl is archived (SHA-256: 421f8e6830833211c929e586804e79cb1a001eb8d6a550d0ac19efbc8a979753) and the analysis log analysis/analysis_log.jsonl is archived (SHA-256: 9ea0d56d48a5cc7ff198d85d0a12c21536fab716c042bd5eb2033492eda5b18e). These artifacts document observed provider calls and confirm that 401 model calls were used in this run (400 shared_initial + 1 repair).
- Planned vs observed model calls: the preregistration/execution contract listed a planning budget of 800 model calls under independent_generation assumptions. The observed model_calls_used = 401 is artifact-backed and arises from the preregistered and frozen shared-initial design (independent_condition_generation=false), which deterministically produced one shared candidate per intent that was reused across conditions (therefore 400 shared-generation calls) plus one observed repair call in the guarded stage; this reconciliation is recorded in the execution manifest (see paired_contingency_table.csv and provider_call_audit entries; paired artifact hashes: execution/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 a6906bb4..., execution/transformation_manifest.json SHA-256 ab91e0f1...). Logically, the planned 800-call budget reflected independent-generation counting; the executed shared-initial design is preregistered and produced 401 model calls — we report this as an artifact-backed execution accounting fact rather than a post-hoc deviation. All related provider-call logs and per-episode JSONs are archived and hash-summed in the execution manifest artifact_hashes for inspection.
- Reproducibility: all raw outputs, per-task scorer JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json), response texts (execution/responses/*.txt), provider-call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), result schema, task and transformation manifests, and analysis artifacts (analysis/*.csv, analysis/*.json, analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg) are archived with SHA-256 hashes in the execution manifest artifact_hashes. Representative artifact paths and authoritative SHA-256 values cited in the manuscript include: execution/condition_summary.csv (SHA-256: 0d6efc16e14d92a1989b0f6d7ed80b8bf8579bff5e364b87aeed4cbd075a3d7e), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA-256: a6906bb43712dcf82b3bc8bdc0ef095d228bcdc8a6a857d9cbbba1ad87245af8), execution/execution_log.jsonl (SHA-256: 421f8e6830833211c929e586804e79cb1a001eb8d6a550d0ac19efbc8a979753), and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA-256: 9ea0d56d48a5cc7ff198d85d0a12c21536fab716c042bd5eb2033492eda5b18e). Inspectors may use these artifacts to reproduce the analysis steps and verify the reported counts and hashes.
- Human involvement: after the autonomy lock the manuscript text, analysis, and artifact aggregation were produced autonomously by the agentic pipeline; no human manually edited the technical manuscript content post-lock. Human roles prior to the lock were limited to topic-family selection and prompt constraints as documented in the master prompt archive (provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA-256 above). Pre-lock development and rehearsals produced infrastructure but were explicitly excluded from the confirmatory evidence unless recreated in the post-lock pipeline.
- Missing preregistered telemetry: the preregistered latency hypothesis (H2) required end-to-end timing and 95th-percentile latency telemetry for the pipelines; the confirmatory artifact bundle does not include those telemetry records. This absence is recorded in the execution manifest and analysis logs and prevents artifact-verified evaluation of H2; we state this transparently in the manuscript rather than fabricating timing data.
- Limitations and scope: the run used a single LLM (gpt-5-mini) and a single deterministic validator; the confirmatory corpus is synthetic; the shared-initial design focuses inference on verifier/repair effects conditional on a single generated candidate per intent. These are preregistered constraints and are discussed in the manuscript’s Limitations section. All decisions, artifacts, and reconciliations above are archived and hashed in the execution manifest; numerical claims in the manuscript are traceable to those artifacts.
limitations: Synthetic confirmatory corpus: tasks were generated deterministically and may not reflect production diversity or real operator phrasing.
Single LLM: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize across other foundation models.
Single deterministic validator/scorer: safety labels derive from deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (digital-twin semantics); real-device outcomes may differ.

Shared-initial design (independent_condition_generation=false) was preregistered and reduces generation variance between conditions; it isolates verifier/repair effects but narrows the estimand to conditional verifier efficacy given a shared candidate.

Latency SLO (H2) unresolved: end-to-end latency telemetry required to evaluate the preregistered latency hypothesis is absent from the confirmatory artifact bundle and therefore H2 could not be assessed from the archived outputs.
